Evernote for Android

Nielsen Norman Group’s 2015 example of Material Design as “flat 2.0”: a mostly flat app with subtle shadows on the bar and the action button.

Source
Nielsen Norman Group, Kate Moran, “Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users” (27 September 2015)
Creator
Evernote Corporation
Made
c. 2015 (as shown by NN/g)
Style
Material Design (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Orderly, calm
Evidence
Relies on the NN/g article text. Its screenshot of the app is only 512 × 446 px, too small to record visual detail.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

NN/g calls “Google’s Material design language” “one example of flat 2.0 with the right priorities”, and says that the Evernote app for Android “provides a few subtle shadows on the navigation bar and the floating + button (add new). It also makes use of the card metaphor to display content as flat, layerable panes in a 3D space.” NN/g.

Why it belongs

The article is the clearest statement of how Material relates to flat design: the fills stay flat, and a few shadows return only where they tell the user what can be touched.

What to review next

  • Find a larger, dated image of the 2015 Android app, for example in a Wayback copy of evernote.com, before marking this reference observed.
